name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Copilot Chat reaches shared inboxes, Teams pages and Markdown are on the way, school IT gets a tidier WinGet, and Telnet and old Java versions head out.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 05:22 AEDT, Fri 27 Nov 2026 (Wednesday 25 to Thursday 26 Nov in the US, Thanksgiving).
notes: A quiet US Thanksgiving: no new Microsoft Education posts or [Education] roadmap items in the window, so today's stories are campus-wide updates framed for schools and universities. This week: GitHub's 'Art of play' post (25 Nov, 16:00 UTC); WinGet 1.30's release candidate came out on 24 Nov, with press coverage in the window.

Status: Copilot Chat in shared mailboxes is rolling out; Pages in Teams (January) and expanded Markdown in Teams (December preview) are roadmap items in development; WinGet 1.30 is a release candidate; Excel's accounting skills are in the Frontier early-access program.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 27 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
TIDY UP. 🧹

The last 24h at Microsoft for education:
- Copilot Chat in shared and delegate inboxes (rolling out)
- Pages you can edit together in Teams (due Jan)
- WinGet keeps installing when an app's missing (preview)
- Telnet Client on its way out of Windows
post.alt: A 3-minute motion-graphics showreel of Microsoft updates for education (27 Nov 2026): Copilot Chat in shared and delegate mailboxes in classic Outlook, Pages in Teams, more Markdown in Teams, WinGet 1.30's release candidate, Microsoft's guide to Copilot Studio agent costs, accounting skills in Copilot in Excel, GitHub's change to Copilot code review billing, the deprecation of Windows' Telnet Client, the end of Java 8, 11 and 17 support in Azure Functions, Xbox Free Play Days and GitHub's 'Art of play' post, with captions, sources and article screenshots.

stories.title: Copilot Chat comes to shared and delegate mailboxes in classic Outlook
stories.summary: Shared mailbox users and delegates with full access or folder-level permission can now use Copilot Chat right from those mailboxes in classic Outlook, once the mailbox is added as a resource. It's rolling out, with general availability listed for November 2026. A school office's shared inbox is our example.
stories.for: School office staff and delegates managing inboxes

stories.title: Pages shared in Teams chats and channels will open right in Teams
stories.summary: When someone shares a page in a chat or channel, you'll be able to open it in Teams, in the main window or a new one, then edit it and discuss it with others. It's a roadmap item in development, with preview and general availability due January 2027. Student group projects are our example.
stories.for: Teachers and students working together in Teams

stories.title: Teams is getting more Markdown in the compose box
stories.summary: Teams is expanding Markdown support in the compose box, so you can structure and format messages with familiar Markdown syntax. It's a roadmap item in development, with a preview due in December 2026 and general availability in January 2027. Coding classes are our example.
stories.for: Coding classes and anyone who formats messages

stories.title: WinGet 1.30's release candidate keeps installing when one app is missing
stories.summary: Windows Package Manager 1.30.310, a release candidate published on 24 November, adds an --ignore-unavailable flag so a multi-app install carries on when one package isn't found, and an experimental option that shows numbered choices when a name matches several packages. Setting up lab PCs is our example.
stories.for: School IT setting up lab and classroom PCs

stories.title: Microsoft's guide to keeping Copilot Studio agent costs in check
stories.summary: Makers can see estimated credits while they build, test and evaluate an agent, and admins can set aside credits per environment, cap an individual agent and get alerts near capacity. Microsoft now recommends Agent 365 cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center, with identity-scoped policies coming soon.
stories.for: University IT and teams building AI agents

stories.title: Copilot in Excel gets accounting skills for reconciliations and journal entries
stories.summary: Through the Frontier early-access program, Copilot in Excel and Cowork can reconcile accounts and prepare reconciling items for you to review, draft journal entries such as accruals and reversals, and explain performance against plan. GPT-6.2 Sol is also now in the model picker in Copilot in Excel.

stories.title: GitHub will bill Copilot code reviews to the organization from 30 December unless you choose Member
stories.summary: For organizations and enterprises on Copilot Business or Enterprise that haven't chosen how to bill Copilot code review for licensed members, reviews will be billed to the organization from 30 December 2026. Select Member before then to keep using members' own Copilot; organization billing needs AI Credits paid usage and can raise spending.
stories.for: University GitHub admins on Copilot Business or Enterprise

stories.title: Windows' Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed
stories.summary: Microsoft has added Telnet Client (telnet.exe) to its list of deprecated Windows features: it's no longer being developed and will be removed in a future release, with no date yet. It's an optional feature that isn't installed by default, BetaNews notes. Scripts and networking lab guides that still use it are our example.
stories.status: Deprecated; removal in a future release

stories.title: Azure Functions support for Java 8, 11 and 17 ends on 1 September 2027
stories.summary: Apps on Java 8, 11 and 17 will keep running on Azure Functions after 1 September 2027, but they'll no longer get security updates or customer support. Microsoft says to upgrade function apps to Java 25 before then.
stories.for: Campus developers and student projects on Azure

stories.title: Little Rocket Lab and Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus are free to play on Xbox this weekend
stories.summary: Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and Essential members can play both games free from Thursday 26 to Sunday 29 November. Little Rocket Lab has you build factories and finish a rocket ship, and it's 30% off; Warhammer 40,000: Mechanicus is 90% off until 7 December. Discounts vary by region.
stories.for: Students and staff with Game Pass, after hours
stories.status: Free to play until Sunday 29 November

stories.title: GitHub: give yourself permission to play, and call it learning
stories.summary: In 'Art of play in the age of AI', GitHub says AI makes room to experiment again, quoting Martin Woodward: give yourself permission to play, call it learning, and time-box it. Its hackable Universe badges now have a colour screen, motion sensors and game controls; he trained a simple model in his browser to make his a pedometer.
stories.for: Student coders and computer science classes

transcript.t: Welcome to the Microsoft for Education Daily, Friday edition.
Here's what shipped at Microsoft in the last 24 hours.
Time to tidy up the office inbox: Copilot Chat is rolling out to shared mailboxes in classic Outlook.
Delegates get it too: run the principal's inbox, and Copilot's right there.
For classes, a page shared in a Teams chat or channel will open right in Teams, due January.
Edit it together and talk it through in t he same window: handy for group projects.
Teams is also getting more Markdown in the compose box, with a preview due in December.
Good news for coding classes: format messages the way you'd write a README file.
School IT building lab PCs?
WinGet's new release candidate can keep installing when one app is missing.
And when one name matches several apps, an experimental prompt lets you pick by number.
Building AI agents on campus?
Microsoft's new guide shows how to keep Copilot Studio costs in check.
Makers see estimated credits as they build, and admins can cap each agent and get alerts.
Something calmer for the finance office: Copilot in Excel can now reconcile accounts, in early access.
It drafts journal entries and explains what changed against the plan, all ready for you to review.
The fine print? From December 30, GitHub bills Copilot code reviews to your organization, unless you pick Member.
Also on the way out: Windows' Telnet Client, and Java 8, 11 and 17 on Azure Functions.
After hours on Xbox, Game Pass members can play Little Rocket Lab free until Sunday.
And GitHub's advice for coders, students included: give yourself permission to play, and call it learning.
Four years in, its conference badges have colour screens and game controls; one even became a pedometer.
Old tools out, budgets clear, a little play: a good week to tidy up.
Every day, the changelog gets a little longer.
On the release board: shipped, and still shipping.
That was 24 hours at Microsoft. Tomorrow, there's more.
That's the Microsoft for Education Daily for today.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
